title: 2026 North Carolina State Senate Election Results
text:
An analysis of the November 2026 North Carolina State Senate legislative election across all 50 districts.

In the 2026 general election, control of the North Carolina State Senate was closely contested. Out of the 50 total senate seats, Republicans won 26 seats and Democrats won 24 seats.
The map below illustrates each district’s election outcome. Districts are shaded by the margin of victory, with blue indicating Democratic victories and red indicating Republican victories.

title: About
text:
Unlike congressional or state legislative elections that are decided by specific districts, U.S. Senate races in North Carolina are statewide contests. Every registered voter in all 100 counties casts a ballot in the same race.
North Carolina is one of the nation’s premier battleground states, characterized by closely divided statewide results between Democrats and Republicans.

section: What It Takes to Win Statewide in North Carolina
text:
What It Takes to Win Statewide in North Carolina
Winning a statewide race in North Carolina generally requires balancing three key geographic and demographic dynamics:

Urban and Suburban Margins: Candidates from the Democratic coalition typically rely on running up large voter margins in high-density population centers such as Mecklenburg County (Charlotte), Wake County (Raleigh), and the Research Triangle.
Rural and Exurban Strength: Candidates from the Republican coalition generally rely on strong turnout and commanding victory margins across North Carolina’s rural and small-town counties.
Winning Unaffiliated Voters: Unaffiliated voters make up the largest and fastest-growing group of registered voters in North Carolina. Any successful statewide candidate must appeal to moderate swing voters outside the party bases.

title: North Carolina Senate History: Female vs. Male Matchups
text:
Exploring electoral patterns in North Carolina statewide races featuring a female candidate running against a male candidate.

In North Carolina electoral history, several high-profile U.S. Senate races have featured a female candidate facing a male opponent. Most recently in 2022, former North Carolina Supreme Court Chief Justice Cheri Beasley (Democrat) became the first Black woman nominated for U.S. Senate in the state, running against Ted Budd (Republican).
The interactive map below allows you to compare county-level outcomes in the 2022 woman-vs-man contest against the 2026 contest. Use the layer selector in the top-right corner to toggle between elections, and hover over any county to inspect candidate vote shares and victory margins.
